4. What Went Wrong — Honest Audit

4.1 v5 SIGNAL_FLIP Problem (51% Premature Exits)

Critical Issue: 23 out of 45 non-SL trades in v5 exited via SIGNAL_FLIP (51%). On a BULL day, trends are sustained — flipping on a minor retracement kills alpha. Stocks like ADANIPOWER, ADANIENSOL repeatedly re-entered the same direction after SIGNAL_FLIP exits, confirming the flip was premature.
Exit ReasonCount% of TradesAvg P&LAssessment
TARGET3857.6%Rs ~380CORRECT
SIGNAL_FLIP2334.8%Rs ~120PREMATURE in BULL
STOPLOSS57.6%Rs -25ACCEPTABLE
Evidence: ADANIPOWER entered 4 times: 09:55, 13:45, 13:57, 15:03. Between 09:55 and 13:45, there was a 3.5-hour gap where v5 had NO position in this stock despite it trending upward +3.4% on the day. The engine exited via SIGNAL_FLIP and then failed to re-enter until the afternoon batch. Lost approximately Rs 800-1000 in that window per position.

4.2 Under-trading in BULL (0 Open Positions Mid-Day)

Gap: Between 10:15 AM and 11:55 AM, v5 had only 1 trade (NTPC at 11:55). The engine's scan mechanism found 24 candidates across the day but concentrated all entries in morning (9:25), mid-morning (9:55), and afternoon (13:45, 13:57) batches. A full 90 minutes of peak BULL trend momentum was missed completely.

4.3 Rust Engine Shared State Blocked v5.5 at Market Open

Architecture Issue: The Rust risk engine maintains a SHARED position limit counter (max 30 positions) across ALL engines. When v5 and v5.4 both ran simultaneously at 09:25, they collectively hit the 30-position limit, causing the risk engine to reject v5.5 deployment requests. v5.5 could only start once afternoon positions cleared. Fix: implement per-engine position counters (e.g., HashMap<EngineId, PositionCounter>).

4.4 v5.3 Still 0 Trades (Volume Filter)

v5.3 Dead Engine: v5.3 generated 60 signal candidates during the day but all were cancelled by its 0.8x average volume threshold filter. This threshold is calibrated for afternoon liquidity patterns but is too aggressive before 10:00 AM when institutional block trades are still settling. 60 signals wasted = ~Rs 15,000-18,000 of missed alpha (estimated at Rs 250/signal).

4.5 No Shorts Deployed on Any Engine

Missed Opportunity: On a BULL day with +1.9% Nifty, shorts are counter-productive. However, there were 3-4 weak sectors (Pharma, select IT midcaps) that showed negative divergence. All 4 active engines ran 100% LONG-only today. No shorts = correct decision for day-level call, but intra-day shorts on diverging sectors could have added Rs 3,000-5,000.

5. What We Could Have Done Better

1. BULL-Aware Exit Logic from Day Start: v5.5 proved BULL-aware exits work (96% WR vs 94% for v5). v5 should have used regime-conditional exit thresholds from market open. In BULL regime, SIGNAL_FLIP exits should require 2+ consecutive flip signals, not just 1. Fix: add if regime == 'BULL': min_flips = 2 in exit logic.
2. Per-Engine Rust Position Tracking: The shared 30-position counter is a monolithic design flaw. With 4+ engines running simultaneously, a shared counter means Engine A's positions block Engine B's entries. Solution: HashMap<String, Arc<AtomicU32>> keyed by engine_id in the Rust risk module.
3. v5.3 Time-Based Volume Threshold: Static 0.8x volume filter cancels all pre-10AM signals. Fix: time-based multiplier — 0.5x before 10:00 AM, 0.8x after 10:00 AM. This would have allowed ~30 of 60 signals through in the morning session alone.
4. v5.5 Should Have Started at Market Open: v5.5's BULL-aware logic was ready. The only blocker was the Rust shared state issue. With per-engine counters (fix #2 above), v5.5 would have run from 09:15. Estimated additional P&L: Rs 11,000-14,000 (based on 35-40 additional morning trades at Rs 312 avg).
5. v4's Lesson — Absolute Thresholds in BULL: v4 led all engines today (+Rs 21,682) using simple absolute entry/exit thresholds. Its 54% win rate but large average winner shows the BULL market "just hold longer" principle works. Consider a "BULL hybrid" mode for v5 that adopts v4's holding logic when regime = BULL.

14. Watchdog Findings

WATCHDOG-001: SIGNAL_FLIP Dominance in BULL Regime
23 of 66 trades (34.8%) exited via SIGNAL_FLIP. In BULL regimes, signal flips are predominantly noise — price tends to revert in original direction within 2-3 candles. The engine needs regime-conditional exit patience. Recommended fix: minimum 2 flip signals before exit in BULL.
WATCHDOG-002: Under-Trading in Peak Trend Hours (10:15-13:00)
The 9:55 batch generated only 10 trades. After that, no trades until 11:55 (NTPC only) and then 13:45. In a +1.9% Nifty day, momentum stocks were trending for the full session. The scoring/rescore mechanism may have de-ranked previously-entered stocks, preventing re-entry into continuing trends.
WATCHDOG-003: Re-entry Logic Missing for Trend Continuation
ADANIPOWER exited at 09:55 via TARGET, re-entered at 13:45 (4h gap). Same stock, same direction, +3.4% day. The engine has no "trend continuation re-entry" mechanism — once a stock hits target, it's deprioritized even if the trend is intact. Fix: after TARGET exit, re-score the stock at next scan if regime = BULL.
WATCHDOG-004: v4 Outperformance Analysis
v4 ran 117 trades (vs 66 for v5) and earned Rs 21,682. Its TIME_EXIT strategy (44 trades = 38%) held positions through intra-day volatility and let gains compound. This is fundamentally a longer-hold strategy that v5's signal-flip exits counteract. In BULL regimes, v4's time-based exits are superior to v5's signal-based exits.

16. Learnings & Tomorrow's Plan

16.1 What to Train ML On

  • SIGNAL_FLIP Label: For each flip-exited trade, record whether price continued in original direction within 10 min (ground truth for ML feature: "flip was premature"). Target: 60%+ accuracy on identifying false flips.
  • Regime-Exit Correlation: Train a regime-conditioned exit timing model. Features: regime, time of day, sector momentum, volume. Label: optimal hold bars.
  • Re-entry Timing: For stocks exiting via TARGET, record whether re-entry was optimal. Use to train "trend continuation re-entry" classifier.
  • v4 vs v5 Hold Length: Compare average hold bars for v4 (TIME_EXIT dominant) vs v5 (SIGNAL_FLIP dominant) and correlate with final P&L in different regimes.
